dimensions.assessment: Directly affects the Quinault Indian Nation, the Department of the Interior, and the U.S. Forest Service regarding a specific 72-acre parcel.
dimensions.evidence: approximately 72 acres of land located in the State of Washington... taken into trust for the benefit of the Quinault Indian Nation

dimensions.assessment: Brings a specific 72-acre parcel into tribal trust status, making it part of the reservation while preserving existing easements and rights.
dimensions.evidence: shall be part of the Quinault Indian Reservation; and (2) administered by the Secretary of the Interior

dimensions.assessment: No significant federal spending or revenue implications are stated, other than standard administrative transfer and disclosure requirements.
dimensions.evidence: shall meet disclosure requirements for hazardous substances... without otherwise being required to remediate

dimensions.assessment: Applies a narrow land transfer and trust acquisition for a single tribe and specific tract of land, prohibiting gaming on the parcel.
dimensions.evidence: The land taken into trust under subsection (a)(1) shall not be eligible for gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act

dimensions.assessment: Permanent change in land status and reservation boundaries.
dimensions.evidence: shall be part of the Quinault Indian Reservation

missing_information: Economic appraisal or valuation of the 72-acre land parcel.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill administratively transfers approximately 72 acres of land from the Forest Service to the Department of the Interior to be held in trust for the Quinault Indian Nation, affecting a specific local property.
